title: Block 1 Practice Test 3
context: Foundations of Medicine, Block 1, Weeks 1 to 4

questions.p: A clinician wants to know whether a new blood test can accurately identify patients with early kidney disease. Which type of clinical decision-making question is this?
o: A diagnosis question
A therapy question
A prognosis question
A harm question
questions.e: Correct: A. Questions about whether a test accurately identifies a condition are diagnosis questions, distinct from therapy (treatment effect), prognosis (future course), or harm (adverse effects) questions.

questions.p: A resident orders an MRI purely because she suspects her attending prefers imaging in similar cases, not because it will change management. Which Choosing Wisely principle is being violated?
o: Only order tests which will change patient management
Do not order tests in anticipation of preceptor preference
Consider the least invasive testing option first
Do not order tests exclusively for the learning experience
questions.e: Correct: B. Choosing Wisely explicitly advises against ordering tests in anticipation of what a preceptor might prefer, which is exactly what is described here.

questions.p: A teenager with several risk factors for substance use has never engaged in substance use himself, which his counselor attributes partly to his strong involvement in competitive sports. Which of the 4 Ps does this sports involvement represent?
o: A predisposing factor
A precipitating factor
A protective factor
A perpetuating factor
questions.e: Correct: C. A protective factor is a strength that reduces the severity or likelihood of a problem, as sports involvement does here, distinct from predisposing, precipitating, or perpetuating factors.

questions.p: A clinic actively redesigns its intake process, hires interpreters, and adjusts scheduling based on specific feedback from immigrant communities it serves. Which stage of the cultural competence continuum does this best reflect?
o: Cultural pre-competence
Cultural blindness
Cultural incapacity
Cultural proficiency
questions.e: Correct: D. Cultural proficiency involves implementing concrete changes to improve services based on cultural needs, going beyond pre-competence (early commitment and assessment) toward active, sustained change.

questions.p: A cancer cell secretes a growth factor that binds receptors on its own surface, stimulating its own proliferation. Which type of cell signalling does this describe?
o: Autocrine signalling
Paracrine signalling
Endocrine signalling
Synaptic signalling
questions.e: Correct: A. Autocrine signalling occurs when a cell signals to itself, as opposed to paracrine (nearby cells), endocrine (bloodstream to distant targets), or synaptic (nerve cell to nerve cell) signalling.

questions.p: Glucose, a large polar molecule, crosses a cell membrane down its concentration gradient using a dedicated carrier protein, without any ATP expenditure. Which transport mechanism is this?
o: Simple diffusion
Facilitated diffusion
Primary active transport
Secondary active transport
questions.e: Correct: B. Facilitated diffusion uses carrier proteins to move larger polar molecules like glucose down their concentration gradient, without requiring ATP, distinguishing it from active transport mechanisms.

questions.p: A drug with very high lipid solubility and small molecular size is compared to a similar drug with low lipid solubility and larger size, both crossing the same membrane area. Which statement is correct?
o: The first drug will diffuse more slowly across the membrane
Molecular size and lipid solubility do not affect diffusion rate
The first drug will diffuse more rapidly across the membrane
Both drugs will diffuse at an identical rate
questions.e: Correct: C. Higher lipid solubility and smaller molecular size both favor faster diffusion across a membrane, so the first drug will diffuse more rapidly than the second.

questions.p: A single fertilized cell divides repeatedly and its daughter cells express different genes, forming distinct tissues such as muscle and nerve, despite an identical genome. Which concept best explains this process?
o: Genomic imprinting
Allelic heterogeneity
Anticipation
Cellular specialization
questions.e: Correct: D. Cellular specialization describes how cells with an identical genome become organized and customized into different tissue types through differential gene expression, distinct from imprinting, allelic heterogeneity, or anticipation.

questions.p: A mother with a mitochondrial disorder has children who are all affected to varying degrees, while an affected father with the same disorder has no affected children. Which pattern of inheritance does this illustrate?
o: Mitochondrial (maternal) inheritance
Autosomal dominant inheritance
X-linked recessive inheritance
Autosomal recessive inheritance
questions.e: Correct: A. Mitochondrial DNA is inherited exclusively from the mother, so an affected mother passes the disorder to all her children in varying degrees, while an affected father transmits it to none of his children, a non-Mendelian pattern.

questions.p: A pedigree shows an inherited condition appearing in every generation, affecting roughly half of each affected parent's children, with both sexes equally affected. Which inheritance pattern is most consistent with this pattern?
o: Autosomal recessive inheritance
Autosomal dominant inheritance
X-linked recessive inheritance
Mitochondrial inheritance
questions.e: Correct: B. Vertical transmission across every generation, roughly 50% of offspring affected, and equal involvement of both sexes describes classic autosomal dominant inheritance.

questions.p: Two unaffected parents who are first cousins have a child affected with a rare metabolic condition, with no other family history. Which inheritance pattern is most consistent with this presentation?
o: Autosomal dominant inheritance
X-linked dominant inheritance
Autosomal recessive inheritance
Mitochondrial inheritance
questions.e: Correct: C. Unaffected carrier parents, consanguinity, and an isolated affected child with no other family history are classic features of autosomal recessive inheritance.

questions.p: A condition affects males far more often than females, is never passed from an affected father to his sons, but can be transmitted through unaffected carrier mothers to their sons. Which inheritance pattern is this?
o: Autosomal recessive inheritance
Autosomal dominant inheritance
Mitochondrial inheritance
X-linked recessive inheritance
questions.e: Correct: D. Predominantly male-affected, no father-to-son transmission (since fathers pass a Y chromosome to sons), and transmission through carrier mothers are hallmark features of X-linked recessive inheritance.

questions.p: While taking a prenatal family history, a physician specifically asks about prior pregnancy losses, known genetic conditions, and consanguinity between partners. Which statement best explains why these specific elements are prioritized?
o: They help identify risk factors that could affect fetal development and guide screening
They are required only for legal documentation purposes
They have no bearing on prenatal risk assessment
They are only relevant for the mother's own future health
questions.e: Correct: A. These specific family history elements are prioritized because they directly help identify risk factors that could affect fetal development, guiding which prenatal screening or genetic counselling options should be offered.

questions.p: A 41-year-old pregnant woman with pre-existing type 2 diabetes is counselled that both her age and her diabetes independently increase risk to her pregnancy. Which statement is correct?
o: Only maternal age affects pregnancy risk, not diabetes
Both factors are recognized as risk factors that can affect fetal or maternal health outcomes
Only diabetes affects pregnancy risk, not maternal age
Neither factor meaningfully affects pregnancy outcomes
questions.e: Correct: B. Both advanced maternal age and pre-existing diabetes are independently recognized risk factors that can affect fetal and maternal health outcomes in pregnancy.

questions.p: A newborn exam reveals a cleft lip and palate along with an unusually small head circumference. Which statement about this combination is most accurate?
o: Cleft lip and palate alone always indicate a chromosomal abnormality
This combination is a normal variant requiring no further work-up
Small head circumference is expected in all newborns with cleft lip
This combination is suggestive of an underlying congenital or genetic syndrome warranting further investigation
questions.e: Correct: D. Multiple congenital anomalies occurring together, such as cleft lip/palate plus microcephaly, are suggestive of an underlying syndrome and warrant further genetic and clinical investigation.

questions.p: A 27-year-old pregnant woman with no personal or family history of genetic conditions asks what screening is routinely recommended for her low-risk pregnancy. Which response is most accurate?
o: She requires immediate referral for genetic counselling regardless of her history
No prenatal screening is recommended without a specific risk factor
Routine first-trimester screening is generally sufficient without additional genetic counselling
Diagnostic testing such as amniocentesis should be offered first-line
questions.e: Correct: C. For a genuinely low-risk pregnancy with no concerning history, routine first-trimester screening is generally sufficient, without the need for genetic counselling referral or first-line invasive diagnostic testing.

questions.p: At a routine well-baby visit, a physician uses a standardized Canadian tool covering growth tracking, developmental milestones, immunizations, and anticipatory guidance in one integrated record. Which tool is this?
o: The Rourke Baby Record
The Nipissing District Developmental Screen
The HEADSS interview
The SNAP-IV rating scale
questions.e: Correct: A. The Rourke Baby Record is the standardized Canadian well-child visit tool that integrates growth tracking, developmental milestones, immunizations, and anticipatory guidance in one record.

questions.p: A caregiver consistently and promptly responds to her infant's cues, provides comfort during distress, and engages warmly during play. Which outcome would this caregiving pattern most likely promote?
o: Insecure-avoidant attachment in the infant
Secure attachment in the infant
Insecure-ambivalent attachment in the infant
Disorganized attachment in the infant
questions.e: Correct: B. Consistent, responsive, and warm caregiving is the caregiving pattern most associated with fostering secure attachment in an infant.

questions.p: A 24-month-old combines two words into simple phrases such as "more juice" and "go car," though sentences are not yet grammatically complete. Which stage of language development does this reflect?
o: Single-word stage, expected around 12 months
Babbling stage, expected around 6 months
Two-word phrase stage, expected around 24 months
Complex sentence stage, expected around 4 years
questions.e: Correct: C. Combining two words into simple phrases without full grammatical structure is characteristic of the two-word phrase stage, expected around 24 months.

questions.p: An infant's weight has consistently tracked along the 25th percentile from birth through 9 months, with no crossing of major percentile lines. How should this pattern be interpreted?
o: This always indicates growth faltering requiring investigation
This indicates the infant is overweight for age
This pattern can only be assessed after 24 months of age
This represents normal, expected growth for this infant
questions.e: Correct: D. Consistent tracking along a single percentile line, without crossing major percentile lines, represents normal expected growth, regardless of which specific percentile the child tracks along.

questions.p: A family considering genetic testing for their child is counselled about both benefits, such as guiding management, and limitations, such as potential uncertain results and psychosocial impact. Which statement best reflects this counselling approach?
o: Genetic testing carries both meaningful benefits and real limitations that should be discussed before testing
Genetic testing has no meaningful limitations once benefits are considered
Genetic testing should never be offered due to its limitations
Genetic testing benefits apply only to adult patients
questions.e: Correct: A. Appropriate genetic counselling reviews both the benefits (guiding management, diagnosis) and limitations (uncertain results, psychosocial impact) of testing before proceeding.

questions.p: A family has a known translocation confirmed by karyotype in one parent, and a rapid, targeted test is now needed to check specifically for that same rearrangement in the fetus. Which technique is most appropriate for this specific follow-up?
o: Whole genome sequencing
Targeted FISH testing for the known rearrangement
A complete blood count
A skeletal survey
questions.e: Correct: B. When a specific chromosomal rearrangement is already known in a family, targeted FISH testing is an efficient, rapid way to check specifically for that same rearrangement in a relative or fetus.

questions.p: One patient has an extra complete copy of chromosome 21, while another patient has a normal chromosome number but a rearranged segment between two chromosomes. Which statement correctly classifies these two findings?
o: The first is a structural anomaly, the second is a numerical anomaly
Both are numerical anomalies
The first is a numerical anomaly, the second is a structural anomaly
Both are structural anomalies
questions.e: Correct: C. An extra complete chromosome is a numerical anomaly (change in chromosome count). A rearranged segment with a normal chromosome count is a structural anomaly (change in chromosome architecture).

questions.p: A physician explains to parents that starting therapy for their child's developmental delay now, rather than waiting for a definitive diagnosis, takes advantage of a period when the brain is most able to form new connections. Which concept underlies this rationale?
o: Intervention timing has no effect on developmental outcomes
Brain plasticity only exists after adolescence
Waiting for a definitive diagnosis always produces better outcomes
Early brain plasticity supports better outcomes with earlier intervention
questions.e: Correct: D. Early childhood brain plasticity, the heightened capacity to form new neural connections, is the rationale for starting intervention as early as possible rather than waiting for a definitive diagnosis.

questions.p: A proposed newborn screening test requires a large volume of blood draw that is difficult to obtain safely from newborns and causes significant discomfort. Which principle of population-based screening does this raise a concern about?
o: The test must be suitable and acceptable to the population being screened
The condition must be treatable if detected early
The condition must be an important health problem
The screening program must be cost-effective
questions.e: Correct: A. A key principle of population-based screening is that the test itself must be suitable and acceptable to the population being screened, a difficult, uncomfortable test raises concern about this specific criterion.

questions.p: Research on early attachment suggests that infants with a secure attachment style tend to show which pattern in their later social development, compared to infants with insecure attachment styles?
o: No measurable difference in later social functioning
Generally better social and emotional functioning in later relationships
Consistently worse social functioning regardless of later experiences
Attachment style has no established link to later development
questions.e: Correct: B. Secure attachment in infancy is generally associated with better social and emotional functioning in later relationships, compared to insecure attachment patterns.

questions.p: A parent gives her infant a very high-dose vitamin supplement beyond recommended amounts, and the infant develops symptoms of toxicity. Which DRI value defines the threshold above which this risk becomes more likely?
o: The Estimated Average Requirement (EAR)
The Recommended Dietary Allowance (RDA)
The Tolerable Upper Intake Level (UL)
The Adequate Intake (AI)
questions.e: Correct: C. The Tolerable Upper Intake Level (UL) defines the highest intake level unlikely to pose a risk of adverse effects, exceeding it increases the risk of toxicity, as described here.

questions.p: After identifying multiple abnormal findings in a preschool child's assessment, a physician organizes preliminary investigations across hearing, vision, medical, genetic, and social domains. Which principle does this multidomain approach best reflect?
o: Only medical investigations are ever needed for a developmental concern
Hearing and vision testing are unnecessary in preschool children
Social domain concerns never require formal investigation
A comprehensive problem list requires investigations tailored to each identified domain of concern
questions.e: Correct: D. A comprehensive developmental assessment requires investigations tailored to each domain identified as a concern, rather than relying on medical investigation alone.

questions.p: A student lists several inheritance patterns and is asked which one does NOT follow classic Mendelian rules of inheritance. Which pattern is the exception?
o: Genomic imprinting
Autosomal dominant inheritance
Autosomal recessive inheritance
X-linked recessive inheritance
questions.e: Correct: A. Genomic imprinting is a non-Mendelian pattern, since expression depends on parent of origin rather than following classic dominant/recessive segregation rules like autosomal dominant, autosomal recessive, or X-linked recessive inheritance.

questions.p: One immune cell recognizes a generic bacterial cell wall component shared by many species, while another recognizes one specific unique protein sequence from a single prior infection. Which arm of immunity does each represent, respectively?
o: Both represent innate immunity
Innate immunity, then adaptive immunity
Adaptive immunity, then innate immunity
Both represent adaptive immunity
questions.e: Correct: B. Recognizing a generic, shared molecular pattern is characteristic of innate immunity (pattern recognition receptors). Recognizing one specific unique sequence from a prior infection is characteristic of adaptive immunity (antigen-specific memory).

questions.p: A physician reviews a list of childhood illnesses and identifies which ones are preventable through routine vaccination in Canada. Which of the following is a vaccine-preventable disease on the routine schedule?
o: The common cold
Viral gastroenteritis from norovirus
Pertussis (whooping cough)
Seasonal allergic rhinitis
questions.e: Correct: C. Pertussis is a vaccine-preventable disease included on the routine Canadian immunization schedule, unlike the common cold, norovirus gastroenteritis, or allergic rhinitis, none of which are prevented by routine childhood vaccines.

questions.p: A lymphocyte lacking antigen-specific receptors detects the absence of normal surface markers on a virally infected cell and kills it directly, without prior sensitization. Which innate immune cell does this describe?
o: A B lymphocyte
A cytotoxic T lymphocyte
A plasma cell
A natural killer (NK) cell
questions.e: Correct: D. Natural killer (NK) cells are innate lymphocytes that kill abnormal cells (such as those lacking normal surface markers) without needing prior antigen-specific sensitization, unlike B cells, cytotoxic T cells, or plasma cells, which are part of adaptive immunity.

questions.p: A family's ability to access pediatric specialty care is limited both by the parents' health literacy and by a citywide shortage of pediatric specialists. Which statement correctly classifies these two barriers?
o: Health literacy is an individual determinant, specialist shortage is a structural determinant
Health literacy is a structural determinant, specialist shortage is an individual determinant
Both are individual determinants
Both are structural determinants
questions.e: Correct: A. Health literacy is a characteristic of the individual/family (an individual determinant), while a citywide shortage of specialists reflects the broader system (a structural determinant).

questions.p: A physician caring for a low-income family with a child needing therapy services connects them with a subsidized community program and writes a letter supporting expedited access. Which principle of family-centered care does this best illustrate?
o: Relying solely on medication as first-line management
Incorporating advocacy and community resources into the management plan
Deferring all non-medical needs to the family without support
Limiting management plans strictly to physical examination findings
questions.e: Correct: B. Connecting a family with community resources and advocating on their behalf directly illustrates incorporating advocacy and community resources into a family-centered management plan.

questions.p: A medical student recognizes that a family's complex social needs exceed what she can address alone and involves a supervising physician and a social worker. Which principle does this best reflect?
o: Attempting to independently resolve all aspects of the case
Avoiding involvement of other team members to maintain continuity
Recognizing professional boundaries and seeking appropriate interdisciplinary support
Deferring the entire case without any initial assessment
questions.e: Correct: C. Recognizing the limits of one's own scope and appropriately involving supervisors and interdisciplinary team members reflects sound professional boundaries and collaborative practice.

questions.p: A physician caring for a newly arrived immigrant family takes extra time to understand their health beliefs, uses a professional interpreter, and avoids assuming the family shares the clinic's default cultural expectations. Which principle does this best reflect?
o: Cultural assimilation of the family into clinic norms
Cultural blindness in the delivery of care
A strictly paternalistic model of care
Culturally responsive care for diverse pediatric populations
questions.e: Correct: D. Actively understanding a family's health beliefs, using interpreters, and avoiding assumptions of shared cultural expectations reflects culturally responsive care for diverse pediatric populations.

questions.p: Two children both display high energy and frequent fidgeting, but only one experiences significant difficulty completing schoolwork and maintaining friendships as a result. Which concept most directly explains why only one child would meet criteria for a diagnosis like ADHD?
o: The total number of hours spent being physically active
The child's overall intelligence quotient
The specific time of day symptoms are most noticeable
The presence of functional impairment caused by the symptoms
questions.e: Correct: D. A psychiatric diagnosis like ADHD requires functional impairment caused by the symptoms, not just the presence of high energy or fidgeting, the child with impaired schoolwork and friendships meets this threshold, the other does not.

questions.p: A clinician distinguishes between a condition primarily affecting physical mobility, one primarily affecting cognitive functioning, and one primarily affecting sensory processing, while acknowledging these categories can overlap in a single child. What does this classification approach best illustrate?
o: All disabilities must fall into exactly one single, non-overlapping category
Disabilities can be categorized by the primary domain affected, though overlap between categories is common
Disability categories are determined solely by a child's age
Physical, cognitive, and sensory disabilities are always mutually exclusive by definition
questions.e: Correct: B. Disability terminology often organizes conditions by the primary domain affected (physical, cognitive, sensory), while recognizing that overlap between categories in a single child is common rather than exceptional.

questions.p: A family of a child with a complex developmental disability is referred to a single site offering coordinated access to multiple pediatric rehabilitation services, such as physiotherapy, occupational therapy, and speech-language pathology, under one roof. Which model of care does this best describe?
o: A single-provider walk-in clinic
An emergency department
A Children's Treatment Centre
A public health unit
questions.e: Correct: C. A Children's Treatment Centre is a coordinated site offering multiple pediatric rehabilitation and developmental services together, distinct from a walk-in clinic, emergency department, or public health unit.

questions.p: One framework for understanding disability focuses on impairment as a problem to be treated within the individual, while another framework emphasizes that societal barriers, not the impairment itself, are what primarily disable a person. Which pairing correctly names these two frameworks?
o: The social model, then the medical model of disability
Both describe the medical model of disability
Both describe the social model of disability
The medical model, then the social model of disability
questions.e: Correct: D. The medical model views disability as a problem within the individual requiring treatment. The social model instead views societal barriers as the primary disabling factor, distinct from the impairment itself.

questions.p: A physician who forms a reasonable suspicion that a child may be experiencing abuse or neglect, based on findings during a routine visit, has which of the following obligations under standard child protection principles?
o: A duty to report the suspicion to the appropriate child protection authority
A duty to independently investigate before taking any action
No obligation to act unless the family confirms the concern
A duty to only document the finding without further action
questions.e: Correct: A. Physicians who form a reasonable suspicion of abuse or neglect have a duty to report that suspicion to the appropriate child protection authority, rather than investigating independently or waiting for confirmation.

questions.p: When determining an adolescent's overall stage of development, a clinician considers pubertal physical changes, emotional and cognitive maturity, and the nature of the adolescent's peer and family relationships together. Which statement best reflects this approach?
o: Only pubertal physical changes determine an adolescent's developmental stage
Adolescent development should be assessed across biologic, psychologic, and social domains together
Peer relationships are irrelevant to assessing adolescent development
Cognitive maturity cannot be assessed until adulthood
questions.e: Correct: B. A comprehensive assessment of adolescent development integrates biologic (pubertal), psychologic (cognitive/emotional), and social (peer/family) domains together, rather than relying on any single domain alone.

questions.p: A physician explains to a colleague that adolescents are more prone to high-risk behaviours partly because brain regions governing impulse control and long-term judgment mature later than those driving reward-seeking. Which concept does this best reflect?
o: Adolescents have fully mature impulse control equal to adults
High-risk behaviour in adolescence is unrelated to brain development
A developmental mismatch between reward-seeking and impulse-control brain maturation
Reward-seeking circuits mature later than impulse-control circuits
questions.e: Correct: C. Adolescent risk-taking is linked to a developmental mismatch: reward-seeking brain circuits mature earlier than the impulse-control and judgment circuits, not the reverse, creating a temporary imbalance.

questions.p: A 7-year-old who has entered the concrete operational stage is better able to understand fairness and rule-based games compared to a 4-year-old still in the preoperational stage. Which statement best explains this behavioral difference?
o: Preoperational thinking is more advanced than concrete operational thinking
Rule understanding is unrelated to cognitive developmental stage
Both stages support identical reasoning about rules and fairness
Concrete operational thinking supports logical reasoning about rules that preoperational thinking cannot yet support
questions.e: Correct: D. Concrete operational thinking supports logical reasoning about rules and fairness in a way that preoperational thinking, which relies more on egocentric and semi-logical reasoning, does not yet support.

questions.p: Research on school readiness has identified several factors that predict whether a child will be ready for the social and academic demands of school. Which of the following is one such recognized predictive factor?
o: Early exposure to language-rich and stimulating environments
The specific month of the child's birth within any calendar year
The number of siblings in the household
The family's preferred grocery store
questions.e: Correct: A. Early exposure to language-rich, stimulating environments is a recognized predictive factor for school readiness, unlike birth month, number of siblings, or unrelated family preferences.

questions.p: A physician assessing a school-age child's behavioural concerns proposes hearing, vision, medical, and social investigations before finalizing a management plan. Why are hearing and vision specifically included in this work-up?
o: Hearing and vision problems are unrelated to behaviour in school-age children
Uncorrected sensory deficits can present as behavioural or learning difficulties
These tests are required only for children suspected of having ADHD
Hearing and vision are assessed only if all other investigations are normal
questions.e: Correct: B. Uncorrected hearing or vision deficits can present as behavioural or learning difficulties in school-age children, which is why they are routinely included in a behavioural work-up rather than reserved for a specific diagnosis.

questions.p: After assessing a child's behaviour, a physician provides the family with general advice about expected developmental changes and strategies to support the child at home, before any formal referral is made. Which component of the management plan does this represent?
o: A therapeutic referral
A social support resource listing
Anticipatory guidance
A follow-up strategy
questions.e: Correct: C. Providing general advice about expected developmental changes and home strategies, ahead of any formal referral, is anticipatory guidance, distinct from a therapeutic referral, resource listing, or follow-up plan.

questions.p: An immigrant family maintains their heritage language, traditions, and social ties almost exclusively, while deliberately avoiding engagement with the customs of their new country. Which acculturation strategy does this represent?
o: Assimilation
Integration
Marginalization
Separation
questions.e: Correct: D. Separation describes retaining the heritage culture while deliberately avoiding engagement with the receiving culture, the opposite pattern from assimilation (adopting the receiving culture only).

questions.p: An adolescent immigrant feels disconnected from both his heritage culture and the culture of his new country, engaging meaningfully with neither. Which acculturation strategy does this represent?
o: Marginalization
Integration
Assimilation
Reactive ethnicity
questions.e: Correct: A. Marginalization describes disengagement from both the heritage culture and the receiving culture, distinct from integration (engaging with both) or the other acculturation strategies.

questions.p: A newborn receives protective antibodies that crossed the placenta from his mother during pregnancy, providing short-term protection without his own immune system producing them. Which type of immunity does this represent?
o: Active immunity
Passive immunity
Adaptive cell-mediated immunity
Innate pattern-recognition immunity
questions.e: Correct: B. Passive immunity involves receiving pre-made antibodies (here, transplacentally from the mother) rather than the individual's own immune system producing them, providing immediate but temporary protection.
